Let me say up front that I don't see people in the MGTOW community expecting sympathy from society. This is not a criticism of MGTOW. I think that if you've really "gone your own way" then you don't care what they think. But there are other men out there who still engage with society and they still sometimes attempt to explain to others the issues men face and they hope for sympathy and understanding in return.

...and that's a huge mistake. It's like showing a shark that you're bleeding and hoping for a hug. There are plenty of examples of this, but I've found a particularly good one - it's a good reminder to us all.

Scott Aaronson is a professor of computer science at MIT. Brilliant, I'm sure, but also painfully blue-pill. He tries hard to be a feminist ally and it's clear he really believes in Feminism. He made a blog post about what MIT did to Walter Lewin - they accused Dr. Lewin of sexual harassment, fired him, and removed all his course material (he had taught there for more than 40 years) from their website. It seems to me that MIT made Dr. Lewin an unperson. It seems quite draconian to me.

But Aaronson's blog post did not defend Lewin. It merely criticized MIT for deleting forty years worth of educational material. In fact, (point 1) he went way out of his way to make it clear that harassment is wrong, mkay.

A woman named Amy posted a comment to Aaronson's blog saying she wanted the lectures taken down. She also attacked Aaronson personally, saying:

Do you have any regular readers who are women? I scrolled through over 50 comments before seeing a woman’s name. Why do you figure that is?

Essentially, she's implying that Aaronson's position (that physics lectures remain online) amounted to hostility toward women and resulted in him having no women readers.

Aaronson replied and once again (point 2) went way out of his way to say that sexual harassment is wrong, mkay. He also linked to an article (point 3) that made the claim that teachers in STEM fields don't accommodate women (that is to say, women are oppressed - essentially, he's pandering to Amy's preferred explanation). And he linked to another of his own blog posts (point 4) where he says that nerds like him need to change their culture to better accommodate women.

Aaronson also says (point 5):

I never once in this discussion tried to deny, excuse, or minimize Lewin’s actions, nor did I question the need to punish him severely for them. ... Do I get any credit from your side?

Emphasis original - see how he's begging for Amy's approval? There's even a smiley face in the original!

Unfortunately, Aaronson also included one paragraph in which he defended nerds. It's just one tiny paragraph. It's less than 80 words. Here it is in its entirety:

At the same time, it seems impossible to believe that male physicists, mathematicians, and computer scientists (many of whom are extremely shy and nerdy…) are committing sexual harassment and assault at an order-of-magnitude higher rate than doctors, lawyers, veterinarians, and other professionals. And yet the latter fields have already reached or surpassed gender parity. From these facts, we conclude that fear of harassment and assault can’t possibly be the main explanations for the paucity of women in STEM fields.

Amy of course ignored everything except this paragraph. In her reply she says that yes nerds are worse than other professions:

some of the gropiest, most misogynistic guys I've met have been of the shy and nerdy persuasion

In my opinion, that claim is just laughably absurd. Aaronson posts a long and detailed response - and I would ask everyone to read this link even if you've skipped some of the previous ones. He repeatedly kowtows to the feminist narrative. He later edited the post adding the parts in bold which include more pleading to feminism. He says that (point 6) he's read a dozen feminist books, and that his favorite is Andrea Dworkin’s Intercourse.

He begins by acknowledging the validity of Amy's experiences, saying "If that’s been your experience, then I understand how it could reasonably have led you to your views." (point 7). But then he goes on to relate his own experiences - and here's the part where you as a MGTOW should take notice. Because even after the seven points that I highlighted above in which he conceded to or otherwise praised feminism, do you think they will be sympathetic to him in return? LOL, no.

You should really read it yourself, but Aaronson describes how all his life he has been afraid of offending women. He says that he was full of self-hatred and ashamed of his own sexuality because of what he was told other men do. He even begged a doctor to chemically castrate him so that he wouldn't accidentally transgress!

Later he makes another blog post in which he tries to make it even more clear what a true feminist ally he is.

And now for the best part. After all of that, here's how one of the most famous feminists, Amanda Marcotte summed up everything that you've just read:

a self-pitying comment ... to a woman who dared suggest that nerd men can sometimes be, you know, sexist. ... I thought that his lengthy diatribe must be nuanced and humane on some level. Much to my surprise, however, it was just a yalp of entitlement combined with an aggressive unwillingness to accept that women are human beings just like men.

Yeah, her whole article is like that. Read it if you like. Remember how Aaronson began by acknowledging the validity of Amy's experiences? Here's how Marcotte begins:

one of the more irritating aspects of "Nice Guy®" anti-feminism, which is the whole "how can men be oppressed when I don’t get to have sex with all the hot women that I want without having to work for it?" whine, one that, amongst other things, starts on the assumption that women do not suffer things like social anxiety or rejection.

And ends with:

Women are failing him by not showing up naked in his bed, unbidden. Because bitches, yo.

There are other examples of similarly hyperbolic responses to Aaronson here: http://slatestarcodex.com/2015/01/01/untitled/ This article is fantastic. Please give it a quick scan.

So there you have it. This is how they respond if you ask for sympathy and understanding - not a lot of sympathy mind you, just a little. This is how they respond to a feminist - a true believer, an ally. He repeated over and over again (I counted seven times) that he agrees with them, accepts their worldview, and wants to do the right thing, and they still characterize him as an entitled piece of shit who hates women.

If you've decided to go MGTOW, then do it. Don't look back over your shoulder, hoping that they'll notice you're gone and wish you were back. They have no sympathy for you. Remember Scott Aaronson. They'll treat you a lot worse than they treated him. MGTOW is a way out, it's not a tactic to get back in.
